rules.title: Ban on using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade or coerce price adoption (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Landlords, property managers and software vendors may not use or distribute shared rent-pricing software that draws on competitor data as part of an agreement to restrain trade. They also may not use or offer such software while pressuring others to adopt the rents or lease terms it recommends. Renters harmed by algorithmic rent-fixing can report it to the Attorney General or sue under the Cartwright Act.
rules.key_value: Unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (used by 2+ persons, uses competitor data) in restraint of trade, or to coerce adoption of its recommended prices or terms
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person or business, including landlords and apartment rental companies, that uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm in California. A common pricing algorithm is a method or software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term. The law covers all products and services, including residential rents, and reaches every rental in California, with no limit by building type.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not 'persons' under the section. Single-firm algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered (per secondary source).
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act remedies. Violations can be prosecuted as crimes (per Legislative Counsel's Digest). A secondary source says that under SB 763 (Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 16755, 16755.1) criminal fines reach the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations, and the greater of $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals. The same source cites civil penalties of up to $1 million in actions by the AG or a district attorney, and treble damages, injunctive relief and attorneys' fees in private suits.
rules.reason: Merged subsections (a) and (b) of § 16729 from the official statute text with a law-firm summary of the same AB 325 provision. The conduct-based condition (using a pricing algorithm) was removed from coverage, and the effective date comes only from the secondary source.
